info.title: Unipile API
info.summary: Unified API for messaging, calendars, emails and socials.
info.description:
Unipile API v2. All requests use HTTPS and are authenticated with an API key sent in the `X-API-KEY` header.

Methods returning lists are paginated with either a `cursor` (send back `next_cursor`) or an `offset`/`limit` pair. Methods API calls are rate limited; see the `x-ratelimit-*` response headers.

Errors follow RFC 7807 (see the `Error` schema).

Generated from https://api.unipile.com/v2/docs/json, completed with the per-endpoint definitions, event types, error and rate-limit pages of https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/reference.

tags.name: Webhook Events
tags.description: Events POSTed by Unipile to your webhook endpoints.

get.description: Returns the Accounts accessible to the API Key in the current Application. Use `account_scope_id` with a Scope ID to return Accounts assigned to that Scope, or `none` to return Accounts without a Scope. Accounts are sorted alphabetically by `name`.

parameters.name: account_scope_id
parameters.description: Filter Accounts by Scope ID, or use `none` to return Accounts without a Scope.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter to return only accounts of the given status.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description:
Filter to return only accounts of the given provider.
        - `mock` is mock.
        - `whatsapp` is WhatsApp.
        - `linkedin` is LinkedIn.
        - `instagram` is Instagram.
        - `facebook` is Facebook.
        - `google` is Google.
        - `outlook` is Outlook.
        - `telegram` is Telegram.
        - `imap` is IMAP.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Filter to return only accounts matching the given search term on `name` or `id`.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: A non-negative integer offset used for pagination.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: A positive integer limit of items to be returned.

get.description: Retrieve an Account. After successful Hosted Auth authentication with initial sync waiting enabled, the consumed session can retrieve only its linked account until its polling deadline.

account_scope_id.description: The Scope to permanently assign to an unscoped Account. This field requires a Service API Key, and the Scope cannot be removed or replaced after assignment.

metadata.description: Custom key-value data for the account. Replaces the account `metadata.custom_data` field; other metadata fields are not modified. Any fields not provided will be removed.

auto_proxy_country.description: The rotation country to use for Automatic Proxy Protection. Choose from the countries where Unipile offers automatic proxies. A proxy may be temporarily unavailable even in a country included in the offering.

allow_country_fallback.description: Whether Automatic Proxy Protection may use an available proxy from another country when none is available in the rotation country, during authentication and throughout the account lifetime. Defaults to true. An explicitly selected rotation country must be part of Unipile’s proxy offering for the provider, but a proxy may still be temporarily unavailable there. If false, authentication fails when no proxy is available in the rotation country; if the selected proxy later fails without an available replacement there, the account enters Service interruption.

proxy.description: A new proxy configuration for the account. This will restart the account. Set to `null` to remove the proxy. Removing the proxy will revert the account to using Automatic Proxy Protection if required for the provider.

anyOf.title: Custom proxy
anyOf.description: A custom proxy used to connect to the account provider. When Automatic Proxy Protection applies to the provider, Unipile manages the proxy by default. A custom proxy overrides Automatic Proxy Protection. Read more in the Proxy documentation.

host.description: The hostname or IP address of the proxy, without a scheme, port, path or credentials. Enclose IPv6 addresses in brackets.

port.description: The port of the proxy, between 1 and 65535.

username.description: The username to connect to the proxy. Omitted, null or empty credentials select unauthenticated access when both credentials are absent. SOCKS5 requires both a non-empty username and password for authentication, each at most 255 bytes.

password.description: The password to connect to the proxy. Omitted, null or empty credentials select unauthenticated access when both credentials are absent. SOCKS5 requires both a non-empty username and password for authentication, each at most 255 bytes. HTTP Basic authentication permits an empty username or password.

protocol.description:
The protocol of the proxy. Defaults to `https`.
        - `https` is HTTPS.
        - `http` is HTTP.
          - `socks5` is SOCKS5.
          - `socks4` is SOCKS4.

post.description: Request a full history synchronization for an Account, including after an earlier synchronization completed. Currently supported for WhatsApp accounts. The response confirms that the request was sent; completion is asynchronous and the history returned depends on the provider. An active synchronization prevents another request until it completes or an error is detected.

post.description: Solve the current checkpoint for the given authentication intent.

code.description: The code to solve the checkpoint. Check the AuthenticationCheckpoint response you have already obtained to see what type of code is expected.

credential.description: The secret that goes with the chosen option, when the checkpoint asks for one. On ENCRYPTED_HISTORY, `code` names the option and this carries the PIN or the recovery code; it is left out when the option needs no secret.

intent_id.description: The ID of the intent for which a checkpoint must be solved.

import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

with unipile.ApiClient(configuration) as api_client:
    custom_auth_api = unipile.CustomAuthApi(api_client)

anyOf.title: Checkpoint
anyOf.description: Authentication requires another step or has stopped and cannot continue.

checkpoint.description: The next authentication step, or a notice that the current attempt cannot continue.

anyOf.title: One-Time Password
anyOf.description: A one-time password was sent to the user's phone or email address. The user needs to enter the code in the next checkpoint.

channel.description: The channel the one-time password was sent through, when known.

anyOf.title: In App Validation
anyOf.description: A notification was sent to the user's phone. The user needs to validate the notification by clicking on the link in the notification.

code.description: For number-matching approvals: the digits shown here that the user must select among the choices in their notification.

anyOf.title: Pairing Code
anyOf.description: A pairing code must be entered in the provider app to complete authentication.

code.description: The pairing code to enter on the phone to link the device.

anyOf.title: Phone Register
anyOf.description: The user needs to register their phone number so an OTP can be sent.

anyOf.title: Two Factor Authentication
anyOf.description: The user needs to enter the code generated by the Authenticator App used to setup 2FA or received by SMS.

platform.description:
The platform of the 2FA.
          - `SMS` means the code was sent in a SMS.
          - `APP` means the user must enter the code generated by the Authenticator App used to setup 2FA.
          - `WHATSAPP` means the code was sent via WhatsApp.

anyOf.title: Captcha
anyOf.description: The user needs to solve a captcha checkpoint.

public_key.description: The public key of the CAPTCHA. This is used to verify the CAPTCHA.

data.description: The data of the CAPTCHA. This is used to verify the CAPTCHA.

anyOf.title: OTP or In App Validation
anyOf.description: The user can either enter a one-time password sent to their phone/email or validate a notification sent to their phone.

channel.description: The channel the one-time password was sent through, when known.

anyOf.title: Contract Selection
anyOf.description: The user must pick a contract from a list to activate the correct features and complete authentication.

contracts.description: A list of contracts to choose from.

id.description: The ID of the contract.

anyOf.title: Consent Screen
anyOf.description: The user must select the products that will be activated on the account.

products.description: A list of products to choose from.

id.description: The ID of the product.

display_name.description: The display name of the product.

description.description: What the product gives access to, shown under its name.

icon_url.description: An image of the product's own (e.g. a Page's picture), shown instead of the provider icon.

anyOf.title: Challenge Selection
anyOf.description: The user must pick which alternative verification method to use to receive their code.

challenges.description: A list of alternative verification methods to choose from.

id.description: Identifier of the method (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP or any agnostic ID). Send it back as the `challenge` field of Request Checkpoint to switch to this method.

label.description: Human-readable name of the method (e.g. "WhatsApp", "Text message", "Email").

description.description: Extra detail about the method, e.g. the masked destination the code will be sent to.

anyOf.title: Loading
anyOf.description: The authentication is continuing in the background and requires no user input.

anyOf.title: Passkey
anyOf.description: An additional passkey verification required to finish linking this account. Poll the checkpoint with an empty code; confirm only with CONFIRM followed by a colon and the exact displayed comparison code. CANCEL abandons this attempt.

type.description: An owner-authorized browser verification is required.

stage.description: Whether to verify in the browser or compare and approve the mobile confirmation.

request_id.description: Opaque identifier of this single-use verification step.

expires_at.description: Expiry of this verification attempt, in ISO 8601 format.

comparison_code.description: Compare this code with the code on your phone before approving.

handoff.description: Install or update UniLogin, then authorize this browser verification. No provider session is exported.

request_id.description: Identifier used by the extension bridge.

handoff_token.description: Short-lived capability for this verification; pass only to the trusted extension bridge.

extension_code.description: Code to enter in UniLogin when automatic extension detection is unavailable.

expires_at.description: Expiry of the extension handoff, in ISO 8601 format.

extension_bridge_url.description: Trusted UniLogin bridge URL for this attempt.

extension_download_urls.description: Official extension download links, for browsers without a store listing.

unavailable.description: The verification service is not ready; retry after its update. Ordinary authentication methods remain available.

anyOf.title: UniLogin
anyOf.description: Complete authentication in the browser extension, then poll the connection using intent_id as the account identifier.

type.description: Authentication must be completed through the browser extension.

extension_code.description: Temporary code to enter in the browser extension to authorize this connection.

extension_code_expires_at.description: Expiry of the extension code, in ISO 8601 format.

expires_at.description: Expiry of this connection attempt, in ISO 8601 format.

extension_download_urls.description: Official extension download links, for browsers without a store listing.

anyOf.title: Encrypted History
anyOf.description: The user must choose whether to unlock the end-to-end encrypted message history, and with which credential.

options.description: The ways the user can answer. Send the chosen `id` as the `code` of Solve Checkpoint.

id.description: PIN and RECOVERY_CODE unlock the end-to-end encrypted message history; SKIP leaves it off, and the account then only reports new messages as they arrive.

label.description: Human-readable name of the option.

description.description: Extra detail about what the option entails.

attempts_remaining.description: How many more times this credential may be submitted. Each credential has a budget of its own, starting at 3, so running one out leaves the others open. A PIN is further capped at half of what the provider still allows, so the user can be wrong here without ever being the reason the backup locks. `0` means the option cannot be used any more; absent on options that take no credential.

The most submissions any credential still has — what the user has left overall. `0` means every credential is spent and only skipping remains. The detail per credential is in `options[].attempts_remaining`; a credential the provider refuses to even try does not consume one.

provider_attempts_remaining.description: For a PIN, how many attempts the provider itself still allows before it locks the backup. This budget is the provider's own and is never spent on the user's behalf: when it is unknown or too low, the PIN is refused rather than tried.

last_attempt.description: Why the previous submission did not unlock the history. Absent the first time this checkpoint is served, so its presence is what tells the user their last answer failed.

option.description: PIN and RECOVERY_CODE unlock the end-to-end encrypted message history; SKIP leaves it off, and the account then only reports new messages as they arrive.

error.description: INVALID_CREDENTIAL: the PIN or recovery code was wrong, and one attempt was spent. REFUSED_TO_PROTECT_BACKUP: the PIN was not even submitted, because the provider had too few attempts left to risk one — no attempt was spent, and only the recovery code can unlock the history now.

anyOf.title: Process Stopped
anyOf.description: A terminal outcome for the current authentication attempt. No checkpoint resolution is expected: stop polling and do not call Solve Checkpoint, Request Checkpoint or Resend Checkpoint for this attempt. Use message, description and link to inform the account owner. To retry authentication, start a new authentication attempt rather than continuing the existing intent.

type.description: The current authentication attempt has stopped and cannot be continued or resolved.

message.description: The reason why the authentication attempt cannot continue.

description.description: Additional context or instructions for the account owner, supplementing the main message.

link.description: An optional resource or action to present to the account owner alongside the message.

url.description: An absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL providing information or actions relevant to the stopped attempt.

label.description: The label describing the linked resource or action.

intent_id.description: The ID of the authentication intent. Use it for the next step required by the checkpoint. For PROCESS_STOPPED, it only identifies the stopped attempt and must not be used to resume or resolve it.

anyOf.title: QR Code
anyOf.description: The authentication was started for a QR Code.

intent_id.description: The ID of the auth intent. This should be used to listen for the QR Code scan with Solve Checkpoint.

anyOf.title: Oauth URL
anyOf.description: For Oauth providers (Outlook, Google)

url.description: The URL to redirect to start the oauth flow of the provider.

object.description: The type of the returned object.

user_id.description: The ID of the user that owns the account for the provider.

name.description: The name of the account. This is usually the display name or public identifier (phone number, email address, etc.) of the user that owns the account.

created_at.description: The date and time the account was linked with Unipile.

id.description: ID of the account.

account_scope_id.description: ID of the Scope assigned to the Account. Once assigned, the Scope cannot be removed or replaced.

status.description:
The current status of the account.
    - `running` is Operational.
    - `errored` is Service Interuption.
    - `disconnected` requires authentication.
    - `degraded` means at least one product is running while another is errored; inspect `metadata.products_connection_status`.
    - `partial` means at least one product is running while another requires authentication; inspect `metadata.products_connection_status`.
    Learn more about [Status & Lifecycle](https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/docs/status-lifecycle).

is_locked.description: Whether API access to the account is locked.

provider.description:
The provider's of the Account.
    - `mock` is mock.
    - `whatsapp` is WhatsApp.
    - `linkedin` is LinkedIn.
    - `instagram` is Instagram.
    - `facebook` is Facebook.
    - `google` is Google.
    - `outlook` is Outlook.
    - `telegram` is Telegram.
    - `imap` is IMAP.

oauth_scope.description: If the provider is OAuth, this is the scope of comma-separated permissions granted to the account.

auto_proxy_country.description: The preferred country for automatic proxy selection. A country inferred from an IP may be outside Unipile’s proxy offering. The current proxy may be in another country when fallback is allowed and no proxy is available in the preferred country.

allow_country_fallback.description: Whether an available proxy from another country may be used when none is available in the rotation country, during authentication and throughout the account lifetime. Defaults to true. A country included in Unipile’s proxy offering may still have no proxy currently available. If false, authentication fails when no proxy is available in the rotation country. If the selected proxy later fails and no replacement is available there, the account enters Service interruption. Rotation to another available proxy in that country remains allowed.

connection_method.description: The authentication method that currently owns the account session lifecycle.

v1_account_id.description: The ID of the account in the v1 if the account is migrated from v1.

v1_instance_port.description: The port of the v1 instance from which the account was migrated.

products_connection_status.description: The status of the connection to a product, if the account is connected to multiple products.

products_display_names.description: The human-readable name of a product, keyed like products_connection_status, when the product has one (e.g. the name of a Facebook Page).

custom_data.description: Custom data of the account. This is where you can store custom data using "Update an account" method.

initial_sync.description: Sync details if the account has initial sync enabled.

status.description:
The state of an account’s initial provider sync.
  - `pending`sync hasn’t started yet.
  - `running` sync is currently in progress.
  - `failed` sync could not be completed due to an error.
  - `completed` sync finished successfully.
  .

started_at.description: The date and time the initial sync started.

proxy.description: The proxy used for the account.

country.description: The country of the proxy. If null, the proxy has no defined country.

auto_proxy.description: Whether the proxy was set automatically by Unipile.

host.description: The host of the custom proxy.

port.description: The port of the custom proxy.

username.description: The username used to authenticate to the custom proxy.

protocol.description: The protocol of the custom proxy.

post.description: Request a checkpoint for the given authentication intent. This can be used to request a different type of checkpoint if the first one was not successful.

intent_id.description: The ID of the intent for which a checkpoint must be requested.

challenge.description: The alternative verification method to switch to. Must be one of the `id`s listed in the CHALLENGE_SELECTION checkpoint.

The most submissions any credential still has — what the user has left overall. `0` means every credential is spent and only skipping remains. The detail per credential is in `options[].attempts_remaining`; a credential the provider refuses to even try does not consume one.

provider_attempts_remaining.description: For a PIN, how many attempts the provider itself still allows before it locks the backup. This budget is the provider's own and is never spent on the user's behalf: when it is unknown or too low, the PIN is refused rather than tried.

last_attempt.description: Why the previous submission did not unlock the history. Absent the first time this checkpoint is served, so its presence is what tells the user their last answer failed.

option.description: PIN and RECOVERY_CODE unlock the end-to-end encrypted message history; SKIP leaves it off, and the account then only reports new messages as they arrive.

error.description: INVALID_CREDENTIAL: the PIN or recovery code was wrong, and one attempt was spent. REFUSED_TO_PROTECT_BACKUP: the PIN was not even submitted, because the provider had too few attempts left to risk one — no attempt was spent, and only the recovery code can unlock the history now.

No checkpoint resolution is expected: stop polling and do not call Solve Checkpoint, Request Checkpoint or Resend Checkpoint for this attempt. Use message, description and link to inform the account owner. To retry authentication, start a new authentication attempt rather than continuing the existing intent.

description.description: Additional context or instructions for the account owner, supplementing the main message.

url.description: An absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL providing information or actions relevant to the stopped attempt.

x-code-samples.code:
import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

anyOf.title: Two Factor Authentication
anyOf.description: The user needs to enter the code generated by the Authenticator App used to setup 2FA or received by SMS.

platform.description:
The platform of the 2FA.
          - `SMS` means the code was sent in a SMS.
          - `APP` means the user must enter the code generated by the Authenticator App used to setup 2FA.
          - `WHATSAPP` means the code was sent via WhatsApp.

anyOf.title: Captcha
anyOf.description: The user needs to solve a captcha checkpoint.

public_key.description: The public key of the CAPTCHA. This is used to verify the CAPTCHA.

data.description: The data of the CAPTCHA. This is used to verify the CAPTCHA.

anyOf.title: OTP or In App Validation
anyOf.description: The user can either enter a one-time password sent to their phone/email or validate a notification sent to their phone.

channel.description: The channel the one-time password was sent through, when known.

anyOf.title: Contract Selection
anyOf.description: The user must pick a contract from a list to activate the correct features and complete authentication.

contracts.description: A list of contracts to choose from.

id.description: The ID of the contract.

anyOf.title: Consent Screen
anyOf.description: The user must select the products that will be activated on the account.

products.description: A list of products to choose from.

id.description: The ID of the product.

display_name.description: The display name of the product.

description.description: What the product gives access to, shown under its name.

icon_url.description: An image of the product's own (e.g. a Page's picture), shown instead of the provider icon.

anyOf.title: Challenge Selection
anyOf.description: The user must pick which alternative verification method to use to receive their code.

challenges.description: A list of alternative verification methods to choose from.

id.description: Identifier of the method (EMAIL, SMS, WHATSAPP or any agnostic ID). Send it back as the `challenge` field of Request Checkpoint to switch to this method.

label.description: Human-readable name of the method (e.g. "WhatsApp", "Text message", "Email").

description.description: Extra detail about the method, e.g. the masked destination the code will be sent to.

anyOf.title: Loading
anyOf.description: The authentication is continuing in the background and requires no user input.

anyOf.title: Passkey
anyOf.description: An additional passkey verification required to finish linking this account. Poll the checkpoint with an empty code; confirm only with CONFIRM followed by a colon and the exact displayed comparison code. CANCEL abandons this attempt.

type.description: An owner-authorized browser verification is required.

stage.description: Whether to verify in the browser or compare and approve the mobile confirmation.

request_id.description: Opaque identifier of this single-use verification step.

expires_at.description: Expiry of this verification attempt, in ISO 8601 format.

comparison_code.description: Compare this code with the code on your phone before approving.

handoff.description: Install or update UniLogin, then authorize this browser verification. No provider session is exported.

request_id.description: Identifier used by the extension bridge.

handoff_token.description: Short-lived capability for this verification; pass only to the trusted extension bridge.

extension_code.description: Code to enter in UniLogin when automatic extension detection is unavailable.

expires_at.description: Expiry of the extension handoff, in ISO 8601 format.

extension_bridge_url.description: Trusted UniLogin bridge URL for this attempt.

extension_download_urls.description: Official extension download links, for browsers without a store listing.

unavailable.description: The verification service is not ready; retry after its update. Ordinary authentication methods remain available.

anyOf.title: UniLogin
anyOf.description: Complete authentication in the browser extension, then poll the connection using intent_id as the account identifier.

type.description: Authentication must be completed through the browser extension.

extension_code.description: Temporary code to enter in the browser extension to authorize this connection.

extension_code_expires_at.description: Expiry of the extension code, in ISO 8601 format.

expires_at.description: Expiry of this connection attempt, in ISO 8601 format.

extension_download_urls.description: Official extension download links, for browsers without a store listing.

anyOf.title: Encrypted History
anyOf.description: The user must choose whether to unlock the end-to-end encrypted message history, and with which credential.

options.description: The ways the user can answer. Send the chosen `id` as the `code` of Solve Checkpoint.

id.description: PIN and RECOVERY_CODE unlock the end-to-end encrypted message history; SKIP leaves it off, and the account then only reports new messages as they arrive.

label.description: Human-readable name of the option.

description.description: Extra detail about what the option entails.

attempts_remaining.description: How many more times this credential may be submitted. Each credential has a budget of its own, starting at 3, so running one out leaves the others open. A PIN is further capped at half of what the provider still allows, so the user can be wrong here without ever being the reason the backup locks. `0` means the option cannot be used any more; absent on options that take no credential.

The most submissions any credential still has — what the user has left overall. `0` means every credential is spent and only skipping remains. The detail per credential is in `options[].attempts_remaining`; a credential the provider refuses to even try does not consume one.

provider_attempts_remaining.description: For a PIN, how many attempts the provider itself still allows before it locks the backup. This budget is the provider's own and is never spent on the user's behalf: when it is unknown or too low, the PIN is refused rather than tried.

last_attempt.description: Why the previous submission did not unlock the history. Absent the first time this checkpoint is served, so its presence is what tells the user their last answer failed.

option.description: PIN and RECOVERY_CODE unlock the end-to-end encrypted message history; SKIP leaves it off, and the account then only reports new messages as they arrive.

error.description: INVALID_CREDENTIAL: the PIN or recovery code was wrong, and one attempt was spent. REFUSED_TO_PROTECT_BACKUP: the PIN was not even submitted, because the provider had too few attempts left to risk one — no attempt was spent, and only the recovery code can unlock the history now.

anyOf.title: Process Stopped
anyOf.description: A terminal outcome for the current authentication attempt. No checkpoint resolution is expected: stop polling and do not call Solve Checkpoint, Request Checkpoint or Resend Checkpoint for this attempt. Use message, description and link to inform the account owner. To retry authentication, start a new authentication attempt rather than continuing the existing intent.

type.description: The current authentication attempt has stopped and cannot be continued or resolved.

message.description: The reason why the authentication attempt cannot continue.

description.description: Additional context or instructions for the account owner, supplementing the main message.

link.description: An optional resource or action to present to the account owner alongside the message.

url.description: An absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL providing information or actions relevant to the stopped attempt.

label.description: The label describing the linked resource or action.

intent_id.description: The ID of the authentication intent. Use it for the next step required by the checkpoint. For PROCESS_STOPPED, it only identifies the stopped attempt and must not be used to resume or resolve it.

anyOf.title: QR Code
anyOf.description: The authentication was started for a QR Code.

intent_id.description: The ID of the auth intent. This should be used to listen for the QR Code scan with Solve Checkpoint.

anyOf.title: Oauth URL
anyOf.description: For Oauth providers (Outlook, Google)

url.description: The URL to redirect to start the oauth flow of the provider.

object.description: The type of the returned object.

user_id.description: The ID of the user that owns the account for the provider.

name.description: The name of the account. This is usually the display name or public identifier (phone number, email address, etc.) of the user that owns the account.

created_at.description: The date and time the account was linked with Unipile.

id.description: ID of the account.

account_scope_id.description: ID of the Scope assigned to the Account. Once assigned, the Scope cannot be removed or replaced.

status.description:
The current status of the account.
    - `running` is Operational.
    - `errored` is Service Interuption.
    - `disconnected` requires authentication.
    - `degraded` means at least one product is running while another is errored; inspect `metadata.products_connection_status`.
    - `partial` means at least one product is running while another requires authentication; inspect `metadata.products_connection_status`.
    Learn more about [Status & Lifecycle](https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/docs/status-lifecycle).

is_locked.description: Whether API access to the account is locked.

provider.description:
The provider's of the Account.
    - `mock` is mock.
    - `whatsapp` is WhatsApp.
    - `linkedin` is LinkedIn.
    - `instagram` is Instagram.
    - `facebook` is Facebook.
    - `google` is Google.
    - `outlook` is Outlook.
    - `telegram` is Telegram.
    - `imap` is IMAP.

oauth_scope.description: If the provider is OAuth, this is the scope of comma-separated permissions granted to the account.

auto_proxy_country.description: The preferred country for automatic proxy selection. A country inferred from an IP may be outside Unipile’s proxy offering. The current proxy may be in another country when fallback is allowed and no proxy is available in the preferred country.

allow_country_fallback.description: Whether an available proxy from another country may be used when none is available in the rotation country, during authentication and throughout the account lifetime. Defaults to true. A country included in Unipile’s proxy offering may still have no proxy currently available. If false, authentication fails when no proxy is available in the rotation country. If the selected proxy later fails and no replacement is available there, the account enters Service interruption. Rotation to another available proxy in that country remains allowed.

connection_method.description: The authentication method that currently owns the account session lifecycle.

v1_account_id.description: The ID of the account in the v1 if the account is migrated from v1.

v1_instance_port.description: The port of the v1 instance from which the account was migrated.

products_connection_status.description: The status of the connection to a product, if the account is connected to multiple products.

products_display_names.description: The human-readable name of a product, keyed like products_connection_status, when the product has one (e.g. the name of a Facebook Page).

custom_data.description: Custom data of the account. This is where you can store custom data using "Update an account" method.

initial_sync.description: Sync details if the account has initial sync enabled.

status.description:
The state of an account’s initial provider sync.
  - `pending`sync hasn’t started yet.
  - `running` sync is currently in progress.
  - `failed` sync could not be completed due to an error.
  - `completed` sync finished successfully.
  .

started_at.description: The date and time the initial sync started.

proxy.description: The proxy used for the account.

country.description: The country of the proxy. If null, the proxy has no defined country.

auto_proxy.description: Whether the proxy was set automatically by Unipile.

host.description: The host of the custom proxy.

port.description: The port of the custom proxy.

username.description: The username used to authenticate to the custom proxy.

protocol.description: The protocol of the custom proxy.

post.description: Create a link to the hosted authentication wizard for the user to authenticate with the provider.

anyOf.title: Link new account
anyOf.description: Generate a link to authenticate and link a new account with Unipile.

expires_on.description: The expiration date of the link. Use ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

domain.description: Optional Hosted Auth hostname to use in the generated link instead of the default `auth.unipile.com`. The hostname must already be explicitly verified by Unipile for the parent Application.

redirect_uri.description: The URL to redirect to after the authentication process. If the authentication succeeded, `account_id` and `provider` will be present in query params, along the specified `state`. If the authentication has failed, `error_title` is present instead. This is useful for your app to be aware of the authentication result and to redirect the user to the correct page of your app.

state.description: State data sent as query parameter in the redirect_uri and in the `account.add` / `account.reconnect` webhook payload after the authentication process.

config.description: Specific provider configuration for the hosted auth session.

custom_proxy.title: Custom proxy
custom_proxy.description: A custom proxy used to connect to the account provider. When Automatic Proxy Protection applies to the provider, Unipile manages the proxy by default. A custom proxy overrides Automatic Proxy Protection. Read more in the Proxy documentation.

host.description: The hostname or IP address of the proxy, without a scheme, port, path or credentials. Enclose IPv6 addresses in brackets.

port.description: The port of the proxy, between 1 and 65535.

username.description: The username to connect to the proxy. Omitted, null or empty credentials select unauthenticated access when both credentials are absent. SOCKS5 requires both a non-empty username and password for authentication, each at most 255 bytes.

password.description: The password to connect to the proxy. Omitted, null or empty credentials select unauthenticated access when both credentials are absent. SOCKS5 requires both a non-empty username and password for authentication, each at most 255 bytes. HTTP Basic authentication permits an empty username or password.

protocol.description:
The protocol of the proxy. Defaults to `https`.
        - `https` is HTTPS.
        - `http` is HTTP.
          - `socks5` is SOCKS5.
          - `socks4` is SOCKS4.

oauth_scope.description: The final list of authorizations to request from the Provider. Use this field to expand or narrow the scope of API access. For example, if your application only uses the Calendar API, you may request authorization solely for the calendar, excluding email access for providers like Google. Make sure to give only authorizations accepted by your registered provider application. For a new account, omitting this field requests the authorizations defined in the Provider OAuth settings. For a reconnect, omitting it preserves already granted authorizations and adds the authorizations currently defined in the Provider OAuth settings.

auto_proxy_config.description: Country preferences for automatic proxy assignment. Explicitly selected countries must be part of Unipile’s proxy offering for the provider. If omitted, Unipile determines the preferred country automatically. The fallback setting determines whether an available proxy from another country may be used when no proxy is available in the preferred country.
auto_proxy_config.title: Automatic proxy configuration

country.description: An ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the automatic proxy location, normalized to uppercase. Choose from the countries where Unipile offers automatic proxies. A proxy may be temporarily unavailable even in a country included in the offering.

ip.description: An IPv4 address used to infer the automatic proxy location. If Unipile does not offer proxies in the inferred country, or no proxy is currently available there, allow_country_fallback controls whether an available proxy from another country may be used.

allow_country_fallback.description: Whether an available proxy from another country may be used when none is available in the rotation country, during authentication and throughout the account lifetime. Defaults to true. An explicitly selected country must be part of Unipile’s proxy offering for the provider, even when fallback is allowed. A proxy may be temporarily unavailable in a country included in the offering. Authentication fails if no proxy is available in any allowed country. If false, authentication fails when no proxy is available in the rotation country. If the selected proxy later fails and no replacement is available there, the account enters Service interruption. Rotation to another available proxy in that country remains allowed.

products.description:
Specifies which LinkedIn products are allowed to be activated (as long as the account actually has the relevant subscriptions). By default, all products are made available.
When reconnecting an account, just omit this field to keep allowing access to the same products, or provide new values to expand or narrow the scope. Learn more about Linkedin products `classic` : Personnal Social network
`recruiter` : Recruiter
`sales_navigator` : Sales Navigator
`company` : Company Pages

allow_product_selection.description: When true, show the product selection screen after authentication, even when only one LinkedIn product is available; this screen also displays the requested scopes. When false, products are selected automatically and scope consent is collected before authentication.

allow_methods.description:
The authentication methods to show in the hosted auth.
            `credentials` : Credentials Authentication
            `cookies` : Cookies Authentication
            `unilogin` : Connect the active browser session through the UniLogin extension

surface.description: Meta web surface used to bootstrap the session. `facebook` uses facebook.com/messages (default), `messenger` uses messenger.com.

products.description:
Specifies which Facebook products are allowed to be activated (as long as the account actually has access to them). By default, all products are made available. `messaging` is always activated. `messaging` : Messenger inbox of the account
`page` : Facebook Pages administered by the account — each Page is an inbox (`PAGE__INBOX`) whose chats are answered as the Page

page_ids.description: With the `page` product: the Facebook Pages that can be activated, by id (the Page messaging id, as in `PAGE_<page_id>_INBOX`). By default, every Page the account administers. Without `allow_product_selection` they are all activated; with it, they are the ones offered for selection. Each activated Page runs as its own product `page_<page_id>`, with its own connection status.

allow_methods.description:
The authentication methods to show in Hosted Auth.
          `credentials`: Credentials authentication
          `cookies`: Cookie authentication
          `unilogin`: Connect the active browser session through the UniLogin extension

allow_product_selection.description: When true, show the product selection screen after authentication, even when the account administers no Facebook Page; this screen also displays the requested scopes. When false, products are selected automatically and scope consent is collected before authentication.

Create auth link
x-code-samples.code:
import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

with unipile.ApiClient(configuration) as api_client:
    hosted_auth_api = unipile.HostedAuthApi(api_client)

response = hosted_auth_api.create_auth_link(
    {
    'expires_on': 'value',
    'redirect_uri': 'https://myapp.com/callback',
    'providers': '*',
  }
)

last_message_timestamp.description: The timestamp of the last message in the chat. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

muted_until.description: The date until the chat is muted. Use ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). Is `true` if muted indefinitely.

creator_id.description: The ID of the user who created the chat.

user_id.description: The ID of the other participant in the chat if 1to1 chat.

is_group.description: Is the chat a group chat.

is_channel.description: Is the chat a channel chat.

type.description:
The type of the chat.
    - `group` is a group chat.
    - `1to1` is a 1to1 chat.
    - `channel` is a channel chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the chat pinned at the top of the list, if supported by the provider.

is_readonly.description: Is the chat read-only for the current user. Trying to send messages in read-only chats will fail.

is_archived.description: Is the chat archived. Archived chats are usually hidden from the chat list.

disappearing_messages_timer.description:
The disappearing-message setting for the conversation: `off` when disabled, `seen` when messages disappear after they are seen, or a retention delay in seconds.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the setting.
    This describes the retention of the whole conversation, and is distinct from a message `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

folders.description: A list of folders the chat belongs to.

participants_count.description: The number of participants in the chat if the chat is a group.

unread_count.description: The number of unread messages in the chat. `0` if the chat is read, `-1` if the chat was manually marked as unread by the user and does not have any unread messages.

restrictions.description:
List of action restrictions of the chat.
      - `send_message` is the permission to send messages.

last_message.description: The last message in the chat.

id.description: The ID of the message.

text.description: The text content of the message.

sender_display_name.description: The display name of the sender of the message.

is_sender.description: Is the message sent by the current user.

id.description: The unique identifier of the message for the provider.

text.description: The text content of the message.

sender_id.description: The ID of the user who sent the message.

chat_id.description: The ID of the chat where the message was sent.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the message. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

is_sender.description: Is the current user the sender of the message.

is_hidden.description: Is the message hidden. Hidden messages are usually not displayed in the chat but can be as last message is chats list.

is_seen.description: Is the message seen by other participants.

is_delivered.description: Is the message delivered to the other participants.

is_deleted.description: Is the message deleted. Some providers show the message as deleted in the chat.

is_edited.description: Is the message edited. Some providers adds an "edited" mark on the message in the chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the message pinned. Pinned messages are usually displayed at the top of the chat.

is_starred.description: Whether the account has starred the message. This state is private to the account. Absent when unavailable or unsupported.

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

event_type.description:
The type of message event.
    0 : Unknown (Not implemented)
    1 : Chat name update
    2 : Chat description update
    3 : New participant added to the chat group
    4 : Participant kicked or left the chat group
    5 : A message is pinned
    6 : Permissions have been updated
    7 : Participant was promoted or demoted
    8 : Reaction
    9 : Call Missed
    10 : Call Started
    11 : Call Ended
    12 : Call Rejected
    13 : Scheduled Call Created
    14 : Scheduled Call Cancelled
    15 : Scheduled Call Started
    16 : Announcement
    17 : Content mention

    - `telegram` is Telegram.
    - `imap` is IMAP.

x-code-samples.name: Start chat
Start chat
x-code-samples.code:
import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

with unipile.ApiClient(configuration) as api_client:
    messaging_api = unipile.MessagingApi(api_client)

response = messaging_api.start_chat(
    ACCOUNT_ID,
    {
    'text': 'Hello, world!',
    'users_ids': ['user_id'],
  }
)

is_readonly.description: Is the chat read-only for the current user. Trying to send messages in read-only chats will fail.

disappearing_messages_timer.description:
The disappearing-message setting for the conversation: `off` when disabled, `seen` when messages disappear after they are seen, or a retention delay in seconds.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the setting.

unread_count.description: The number of unread messages in the chat. `0` if the chat is read, `-1` if the chat was manually marked as unread by the user and does not have any unread messages.

is_delivered.description: Is the message delivered to the other participants.

is_deleted.description: Is the message deleted. Some providers show the message as deleted in the chat.

is_edited.description: Is the message edited. Some providers adds an "edited" mark on the message in the chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the message pinned. Pinned messages are usually displayed at the top of the chat.

is_starred.description: Whether the account has starred the message. This state is private to the account. Absent when unavailable or unsupported.

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

event_type.description:
The type of message event.
    0 : Unknown (Not implemented)
    1 : Chat name update
    2 : Chat description update
    3 : New participant added to the chat group
    4 : Participant kicked or left the chat group
    5 : A message is pinned
    6 : Permissions have been updated
    7 : Participant was promoted or demoted
    8 : Reaction
    9 : Call Missed
    10 : Call Started
    11 : Call Ended
    12 : Call Rejected
    13 : Scheduled Call Created
    14 : Scheduled Call Cancelled
    15 : Scheduled Call Started
    16 : Announcement
    17 : Content mention

patch.description: Updates the specified chat by setting the values of the parameters passed. Any parameters not provided will be left unchanged.

name.description: A custom name for the chat. Some providers allow custom names only on groups.

content.description: Content of the file encoded as base64. For large files, prefer using multipart, learn more here: https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/reference/api-usage#sending-files

filename.description: Name of the file (including extension).

duration.description: Duration of the media file.

waveform.description: Waveform of an audio file sent as a voice note, as a list of up to 64 amplitude values between 0 and 100. When omitted, it is computed from the audio file if the provider displays one.

pin_status.description: If supported, set to `true` to pin the chat at the top of the list, or `false` to unpin it.

archive_status.description: If supported, set to `true` to archive the chat, or `false` to move it back to the main inbox.

label.description: If supported, associate the chat with the given label. For Whatsapp, this is resolved by label name and created if missing.

muted_until.description: If supported, the date until which the conversation should be muted. Else `true` to mute the chat for an indefinite time, else `false` to un-mute an already muted chat.

anyOf.description: Must use a supported date-time format. See [supported date formats](https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/reference/api-usage#dates).

read_status.description: Set to `true` to mark the chat as read. This is useful when displaying the list of messages in your app. Set to `false` to mark the chat as unread.

disappearing_messages_timer.description:
If supported, set to `off` to disable disappearing messages, `seen` to make messages disappear after they are seen, or provide the retention delay in seconds.
    Accepted values by provider:
    - WhatsApp: `off`, `86400` (24 hours), `604800` (7 days), `7776000` (90 days).
    - Telegram: `off`, `86400` (24 hours), `604800` (7 days), `2678400` (31 days).
    - Instagram and LinkedIn: updating this setting is not supported.
    The `seen` mode is not currently supported by any provider for this operation.

parameters.name: chat_id
parameters.description: ID of the Chat to update.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: ID of the Account (acc_xxx) to call the method on behalf of.

x-code-samples.name: Update chat
Update chat
x-code-samples.code:
import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

with unipile.ApiClient(configuration) as api_client:
    messaging_api = unipile.MessagingApi(api_client)

response = messaging_api.update_chat(
    'chat_id',
    ACCOUNT_ID,
    {
    'name': 'My Name',
  }
)

id.description: The unique identifier of the chat for the provider.

name.description: The name / title of the chat. If the provider does not provide a name, name is built out of participants usernames.

label.description: If supported by the provider, a label associated with the chat.

description.description: The description / subject of the chat.

public_picture_url.description: Public URL of the chat picture.

private_picture_download_url.description: Private URL to download the chat picture. This URL requires authentication.

image_url.description: The URL of the chat image. Use public_picture_url or private_picture_download_url instead.

created_at.description: The creation date of the chat. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

updated_at.description: The last update date of the chat. Use ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). Some providers update this field on new messages.

last_message_timestamp.description: The timestamp of the last message in the chat. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

muted_until.description: The date until the chat is muted. Use ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). Is `true` if muted indefinitely.

creator_id.description: The ID of the user who created the chat.

user_id.description: The ID of the other participant in the chat if 1to1 chat.

is_group.description: Is the chat a group chat.

is_channel.description: Is the chat a channel chat.

The type of the chat.
    - `group` is a group chat.
    - `1to1` is a 1to1 chat.
    - `channel` is a channel chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the chat pinned at the top of the list, if supported by the provider.

is_readonly.description: Is the chat read-only for the current user. Trying to send messages in read-only chats will fail.

is_archived.description: Is the chat archived. Archived chats are usually hidden from the chat list.

disappearing_messages_timer.description:
The disappearing-message setting for the conversation: `off` when disabled, `seen` when messages disappear after they are seen, or a retention delay in seconds.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the setting.
    This describes the retention of the whole conversation, and is distinct from a message `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

folders.description: A list of folders the chat belongs to.

participants_count.description: The number of participants in the chat if the chat is a group.

unread_count.description: The number of unread messages in the chat. `0` if the chat is read, `-1` if the chat was manually marked as unread by the user and does not have any unread messages.

restrictions.description:

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

post.description: Sets the composing status of the user in a chat.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description:
The composing status of a user in a chat.
    - `typing` if the user is typing / sending a message. This presence must target a chat.
    - `recording` if the user is recording a voice note. This presence must target a chat.

parameters.name: chat_id
parameters.description: ID of the Chat where the composing action is taking place.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: ID of the Account (acc_xxx) to call the method on behalf of.

get.description: Returns a list of messages in a chat. The messages are returned sorted by their timestamp, with the most recent appearing first.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Filter to only return messages sent before the given timestamp (exclusive). Must use a supported date-time format. See [supported date formats](https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/reference/api-usage#dates).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Filter to only return messages sent after the given timestamp (exclusive). Must use a supported date-time format. See [supported date formats](https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/reference/api-usage#dates).

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Filter to only return messages sent by the given User.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: An offset used for pagination, if supported by the provider, else use `cursor`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: A cursor used for pagination. If supported by the provider, use `next_cursor` given by the previous page of the list, else use `offset`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The limit of items to be returned. The maximum allowed value depends on the provider. This is a ceiling, not a guarantee: some providers can return fewer items than requested for a given page.

parameters.name: chat_id
parameters.description: The ID of the Chat to retrieve messages from.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: ID of the Account (acc_xxx) to call the method on behalf of.

id.description: The unique identifier of the message for the provider.

text.description: The text content of the message.

sender_id.description: The ID of the user who sent the message.

chat_id.description: The ID of the chat where the message was sent.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the message. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

is_sender.description: Is the current user the sender of the message.

is_hidden.description: Is the message hidden. Hidden messages are usually not displayed in the chat but can be as last message is chats list.

is_seen.description: Is the message seen by other participants.

is_delivered.description: Is the message delivered to the other participants.

is_deleted.description: Is the message deleted. Some providers show the message as deleted in the chat.

is_edited.description: Is the message edited. Some providers adds an "edited" mark on the message in the chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the message pinned. Pinned messages are usually displayed at the top of the chat.

is_starred.description: Whether the account has starred the message. This state is private to the account. Absent when unavailable or unsupported.

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

event_type.description:
The type of message event.
    0 : Unknown (Not implemented)
    1 : Chat name update
    2 : Chat description update
    3 : New participant added to the chat group
    4 : Participant kicked or left the chat group
    5 : A message is pinned
    6 : Permissions have been updated
    7 : Participant was promoted or demoted
    8 : Reaction
    9 : Call Missed
    10 : Call Started
    11 : Call Ended
    12 : Call Rejected
    13 : Scheduled Call Created
    14 : Scheduled Call Cancelled
    15 : Scheduled Call Started
    16 : Announcement
    17 : Content mention

reason.description: Specifies whether the participant left voluntarily or was removed by an admin.

Sends a message in the specified chat. Use Start a Chat or Start a Chat from Inbox if no conversation has been started with the specified user or group of users yet.

Multipart supported, refer to Sending Files.

text.description: The textual content of first message to be sent. It's recommended not to use HTML or Markdown. To mention a chat participant, write `@` followed by their user ID, as found in `sender_id` or the chat attendees: it is replaced with their name and notifies them where the provider supports mentions. A provider may still deliver the mention as plain text.

quote_id.description: The ID of the Message to quote / reply to.

attachments.description: The list of attachments (uploaded files or a shared post or job) to be sent with the message.

content.description: Content of the file encoded as base64. For large files, prefer using multipart, learn more here: https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/reference/api-usage#sending-files

filename.description: Name of the file (including extension).

duration.description: Duration of the media file.

waveform.description: Waveform of an audio file sent as a voice note, as a list of up to 64 amplitude values between 0 and 100. When omitted, it is computed from the audio file if the provider displays one.

send_mode.description:
Defines how the attachment should be sent, if the provider supports multiple modes.
            Omitted: use the provider’s native default behavior.
            - `file` send as a regular uploaded file.
            - `native` send as a native media (displayed picture, voice note, recorded video, etc.)

voice_note.description: Deprecated compatibility flag for audio attachments. Use `send_mode: "native"` instead.

x-code-samples.name: Send message
Send message
x-code-samples.code:
import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

with unipile.ApiClient(configuration) as api_client:
    messaging_api = unipile.MessagingApi(api_client)

response = messaging_api.send_message(
    'chat_id',
    ACCOUNT_ID,
    {
    'text': 'Hello, world!',
  }
)

id.description: The unique identifier of the message for the provider.

text.description: The text content of the message.

sender_id.description: The ID of the user who sent the message.

chat_id.description: The ID of the chat where the message was sent.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the message. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

is_sender.description: Is the current user the sender of the message.

is_hidden.description: Is the message hidden. Hidden messages are usually not displayed in the chat but can be as last message is chats list.

is_seen.description: Is the message seen by other participants.

is_delivered.description: Is the message delivered to the other participants.

is_deleted.description: Is the message deleted. Some providers show the message as deleted in the chat.

is_edited.description: Is the message edited. Some providers adds an "edited" mark on the message in the chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the message pinned. Pinned messages are usually displayed at the top of the chat.

is_starred.description: Whether the account has starred the message. This state is private to the account. Absent when unavailable or unsupported.

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

event_type.description:
The type of message event.
    0 : Unknown (Not implemented)
    1 : Chat name update
    2 : Chat description update
    3 : New participant added to the chat group
    4 : Participant kicked or left the chat group
    5 : A message is pinned
    6 : Permissions have been updated
    7 : Participant was promoted or demoted
    8 : Reaction
    9 : Call Missed
    10 : Call Started
    11 : Call Ended
    12 : Call Rejected
    13 : Scheduled Call Created
    14 : Scheduled Call Cancelled
    15 : Scheduled Call Started
    16 : Announcement
    17 : Content mention

is_sender.description: Is the current user the sender of the message.

is_hidden.description: Is the message hidden. Hidden messages are usually not displayed in the chat but can be as last message is chats list.

is_seen.description: Is the message seen by other participants.

is_delivered.description: Is the message delivered to the other participants.

is_deleted.description: Is the message deleted. Some providers show the message as deleted in the chat.

is_edited.description: Is the message edited. Some providers adds an "edited" mark on the message in the chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the message pinned. Pinned messages are usually displayed at the top of the chat.

is_starred.description: Whether the account has starred the message. This state is private to the account. Absent when unavailable or unsupported.

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

event_type.description:

    1 : Chat name update

    3 : New participant added to the chat group

    6 : Permissions have been updated
    7 : Participant was promoted or demoted
    8 : Reaction
    9 : Call Missed
    10 : Call Started
    11 : Call Ended
    12 : Call Rejected
    13 : Scheduled Call Created
    14 : Scheduled Call Cancelled
    15 : Scheduled Call Started
    16 : Announcement
    17 : Content mention

is_delivered.description: Is the message delivered to the other participants.

is_deleted.description: Is the message deleted. Some providers show the message as deleted in the chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the message pinned. Pinned messages are usually displayed at the top of the chat.

is_starred.description: Whether the account has starred the message. This state is private to the account. Absent when unavailable or unsupported.

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

    1 : Chat name update
    2 : Chat description update
    3 : New participant added to the chat group
    4 : Participant kicked or left the chat group
    5 : A message is pinned
    6 : Permissions have been updated
    7 : Participant was promoted or demoted
    8 : Reaction
    9 : Call Missed
    10 : Call Started
    11 : Call Ended
    12 : Call Rejected
    13 : Scheduled Call Created
    14 : Scheduled Call Cancelled
    15 : Scheduled Call Started
    16 : Announcement
    17 : Content mention

parameters.description: ID of the Chat to retrieve participants from.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: ID of the Account (acc_xxx) to call the method on behalf of.

get.description: Returns a list of emails in the account mailbox. Emails are returned sorted by their `date`, with the most recent appearing first. Search mode applies when `q`, `from`, `to`, or `any_email` is set. Filter mode applies for browse-only queries (dates, folder scope, read/starred/attachment status).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Full-text search in the email subject and body (case-insensitive, partial match). Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook). Combine with `from`, `to`, or `any_email` to narrow by participant address.

parameters.name: meta_only
parameters.description: Speed up the response by only returning the email metadata. body and body_plain are empty strings, and attachments metadata is excluded.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Return messages sent to the given email address. For Outlook, some messages matching this filter may be missing due to a provider limitation. Use `GET /threads/:thread_id` to retrieve a specific conversation. Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Return messages sent from the given email address. For Outlook, some messages matching this filter may be missing due to a provider limitation. Use `GET /threads/:thread_id` to retrieve a specific conversation. Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook).

parameters.name: any_email
parameters.description: Return messages where at least one of the given comma-separated email addresses appears as a participant (from, to, cc, or bcc). For Outlook, some messages matching this filter may be missing due to a provider limitation. Use `GET /threads/:thread_id` to retrieve a specific conversation. Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Filter to only return emails sent after the given datetime (exclusive). Must use a supported date-time format. See [supported date formats](https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/reference/api-usage#dates).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: An offset used for pagination, if supported by the provider, else use `cursor`.

parameters.name: cursor

Search mode applies when `q`, `from`, `to`, or `any_email` is set. Filter mode applies for browse-only queries (dates, read/starred/attachment status).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Full-text search in the email subject and body (case-insensitive, partial match). Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook). Combine with `from`, `to`, or `any_email` to narrow by participant address.

parameters.name: meta_only
parameters.description: Speed up the response by only returning the email metadata. body and body_plain are empty strings, and attachments metadata is excluded.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Return messages sent to the given email address. For Outlook, some messages matching this filter may be missing due to a provider limitation. Use `GET /threads/:thread_id` to retrieve a specific conversation. Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Return messages sent from the given email address. For Outlook, some messages matching this filter may be missing due to a provider limitation. Use `GET /threads/:thread_id` to retrieve a specific conversation. Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook).

parameters.name: any_email
parameters.description: Return messages where at least one of the given comma-separated email addresses appears as a participant (from, to, cc, or bcc). For Outlook, some messages matching this filter may be missing due to a provider limitation. Use `GET /threads/:thread_id` to retrieve a specific conversation. Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook).
