is_archived.description: Is the chat archived. Archived chats are usually hidden from the chat list.

disappearing_messages_timer.description:
The disappearing-message setting for the conversation: `off` when disabled, `seen` when messages disappear after they are seen, or a retention delay in seconds.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the setting.
    This describes the retention of the whole conversation, and is distinct from a message `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

folders.description: A list of folders the chat belongs to.

participants_count.description: The number of participants in the chat if the chat is a group.

unread_count.description: The number of unread messages in the chat. `0` if the chat is read, `-1` if the chat was manually marked as unread by the user and does not have any unread messages.

restrictions.description:
List of action restrictions of the chat.

text.description: The text content of the message.

sender_display_name.description: The display name of the sender of the message.

text.description: The text content of the message.

sender_id.description: The ID of the user who sent the message.

chat_id.description: The ID of the chat where the message was sent.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the message. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

is_sender.description: Is the current user the sender of the message.

is_hidden.description: Is the message hidden. Hidden messages are usually not displayed in the chat but can be as last message is chats list.

is_seen.description: Is the message seen by other participants.

is_delivered.description: Is the message delivered to the other participants.

is_deleted.description: Is the message deleted. Some providers show the message as deleted in the chat.

is_edited.description: Is the message edited. Some providers adds an "edited" mark on the message in the chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the message pinned. Pinned messages are usually displayed at the top of the chat.

is_starred.description: Whether the account has starred the message. This state is private to the account. Absent when unavailable or unsupported.

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

event_type.description:
The type of message event.
    0 : Unknown (Not implemented)
    1 : Chat name update
    2 : Chat description update
    3 : New participant added to the chat group
    4 : Participant kicked or left the chat group
    5 : A message is pinned
    6 : Permissions have been updated
    7 : Participant was promoted or demoted
    8 : Reaction
    9 : Call Missed

x-code-samples.code:
import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

with unipile.ApiClient(configuration) as api_client:
    messaging_api = unipile.MessagingApi(api_client)

response = messaging_api.start_chat_from_inbox(
    'inbox_id',
    ACCOUNT_ID,
    {
    'text': 'Hello, world!',
    'users_ids': ['user_id'],
  }
)

created_at.description: The creation date of the chat. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

updated_at.description: The last update date of the chat. Use ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). Some providers update this field on new messages.

last_message_timestamp.description: The timestamp of the last message in the chat. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

muted_until.description: The date until the chat is muted. Use ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). Is `true` if muted indefinitely.

type.description:
The type of the chat.
    - `group` is a group chat.
    - `1to1` is a 1to1 chat.
    - `channel` is a channel chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the chat pinned at the top of the list, if supported by the provider.

is_readonly.description: Is the chat read-only for the current user. Trying to send messages in read-only chats will fail.

is_archived.description: Is the chat archived. Archived chats are usually hidden from the chat list.

disappearing_messages_timer.description:
The disappearing-message setting for the conversation: `off` when disabled, `seen` when messages disappear after they are seen, or a retention delay in seconds.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the setting.
    This describes the retention of the whole conversation, and is distinct from a message `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

folders.description: A list of folders the chat belongs to.

participants_count.description: The number of participants in the chat if the chat is a group.

unread_count.description: The number of unread messages in the chat. `0` if the chat is read, `-1` if the chat was manually marked as unread by the user and does not have any unread messages.

restrictions.description:
List of action restrictions of the chat.
      - `send_message` is the permission to send messages.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the message. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

is_hidden.description: Is the message hidden. Hidden messages are usually not displayed in the chat but can be as last message is chats list.

is_seen.description: Is the message seen by other participants.

is_delivered.description: Is the message delivered to the other participants.

is_deleted.description: Is the message deleted. Some providers show the message as deleted in the chat.

is_edited.description: Is the message edited. Some providers adds an "edited" mark on the message in the chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the message pinned. Pinned messages are usually displayed at the top of the chat.

is_starred.description: Whether the account has starred the message. This state is private to the account. Absent when unavailable or unsupported.

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

event_type.description:
The type of message event.
    0 : Unknown (Not implemented)
    1 : Chat name update
    2 : Chat description update
    3 : New participant added to the chat group
    4 : Participant kicked or left the chat group
    5 : A message is pinned
    6 : Permissions have been updated
    7 : Participant was promoted or demoted
    8 : Reaction
    9 : Call Missed
    10 : Call Started
    11 : Call Ended
    12 : Call Rejected
    13 : Scheduled Call Created
    14 : Scheduled Call Cancelled
    15 : Scheduled Call Started
    16 : Announcement
    17 : Content mention

import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

with unipile.ApiClient(configuration) as api_client:
    linked_in_api = unipile.LinkedInApi(api_client)

response = linked_in_api.get_recruiter_search_parameters(
    ACCOUNT_ID,
    {
    'source': 'APPLICANTS',
    'project_id': 'project_id',
    'type': 'SKILL',
  }
)

post.description: Creates a new category in the account mailbox, which can then be assigned to emails through the `categories` field. A category name is unique within a mailbox: creating one with a name already in use returns a conflict.

get.description: Returns a list of emails carrying the specific category, across all the folders of the account mailbox. Emails are returned sorted by their `date`, with the most recent appearing first. Search mode applies when `q`, `from`, `to`, or `any_email` is set. Filter mode applies for browse-only queries (dates, folder scope, read/starred/attachment status).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Full-text search in the email subject and body (case-insensitive, partial match). Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook). Combine with `from`, `to`, or `any_email` to narrow by participant address.

parameters.name: meta_only
parameters.description: Speed up the response by only returning the email metadata. body and body_plain are empty strings, and attachments metadata is excluded.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Return messages sent to the given email address. For Outlook, some messages matching this filter may be missing due to a provider limitation. Use `GET /threads/:thread_id` to retrieve a specific conversation. Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Return messages sent from the given email address. For Outlook, some messages matching this filter may be missing due to a provider limitation. Use `GET /threads/:thread_id` to retrieve a specific conversation. Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook).

parameters.name: any_email
parameters.description: Return messages where at least one of the given comma-separated email addresses appears as a participant (from, to, cc, or bcc). For Outlook, some messages matching this filter may be missing due to a provider limitation. Use `GET /threads/:thread_id` to retrieve a specific conversation. Activates search mode: results may be approximate and non-exhaustive (provider-dependent, ~1000 results on Outlook).

parameters.name: has_attachment
parameters.description: Filter to only return emails with or without attachments. For Outlook with `meta_only=true`, this uses the provider attachment flag, which excludes inline attachments.

parameters.name: is_starred
parameters.description: Filter to only return starred or unstarred emails.

parameters.name: is_unread
parameters.description: Filter to only return unread or read emails.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Filter to only return emails sent before the given datetime (exclusive). Must use a supported date-time format. See [supported date formats](https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/reference/api-usage#dates).

parameters.name: exclude_folder
parameters.description: Filter to only return emails that are not in any of the folders specified in the comma-separated list of folder IDs.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Filter to only return emails sent after the given datetime (exclusive). Must use a supported date-time format. See [supported date formats](https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/reference/api-usage#dates).

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: An offset used for pagination, if supported by the provider, else use `cursor`.

parameters.name: limit

Creates a new story from a single image or video attachment (if supported by the provider).

Multipart supported, refer to Sending Files.

text.description: Optional caption for the story. User mentions can be added by inserting an @ followed by the ID or public identifier of the user (example: @JohnDoe), if supported by the provider.

instagram.description: Specific options to apply if the provider of the targeted account is Instagram

location.description: Location sticker to attach to the story.

name.description: The display name of the location, rendered as the sticker text.

The ID of the Post to retrieve.
Use IDs from *Get a Post*, *Create a Post* or *List all User's Posts* methods responses. IDs from LinkedIn Classic post search responses can also be used directly. Use the returned ID unchanged; access and available actions still depend on the post's permissions. Some providers may allow native Post IDs, please refer to Posts integration guides.

import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

    posts_api = unipile.PostsApi(api_client)

response = posts_api.get_post(
    'post_id',
    ACCOUNT_ID
)

parameters.name: post_id
parameters.description:
The ID of the Post to update.
Use IDs from *Get a Post*, *Create a Post* or *List all User's Posts* methods responses. IDs from LinkedIn Classic post search responses can also be used directly. Use the returned ID unchanged; access and available actions still depend on the post's permissions. Some providers may allow native Post IDs, please refer to Posts integration guides.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: ID of the Account (acc_xxx) to call the method on behalf of.

x-code-samples.name: Update post
Update post
x-code-samples.code:
import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

with unipile.ApiClient(configuration) as api_client:
    posts_api = unipile.PostsApi(api_client)

response = posts_api.update_post(
    'post_id',
    ACCOUNT_ID,
    {
    'text': 'Hello, world!',
  }
)

get.description: Retrieves the specified User profile. Use `me` as `user_id` to specify the owner of the connected account.

allOf.description:
Sections of the profile that should be included in the response (if supported by the provider).
          
  LinkedIn profile sections:
  - `linkedin_*` is for All sections at once.
  - `linkedin_experience` is Experience section.
  - `linkedin_education` is Education section.
  - `linkedin_languages` is Languages section.
  - `linkedin_skills` is Skills section.
  - `linkedin_certifications` is Licenses & certifications section.
  - `linkedin_volunteer_experience` is Volunteer Experience section.
  - `linkedin_projects` is Projects section.
  - `linkedin_recommendations` is Recommendations section.
  - `linkedin_interests` is Interests section.
  - `linkedin_recruiting_activity` is Recruiting activity section (Recruiter only).

  Keep in mind that LinkedIn may throttle sections requests when too many calls are made in a short time. To minimize the risk, you can add the `_preview` suffix to any section that you consider to be less critical. This method returns only the first few visible entries of a given section.

A variant of the profile (if supported by the provider).
          
  LinkedIn variants:
  - `linkedin_classic` is Classic API profile variant.
  - `linkedin_recruiter` is Recruiter API profile variant.
  - `linkedin_sales_navigator` is Sales navigator API profile variant.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The ID of the User to retrieve.

parameters.name: account_id
parameters.description: ID of the Account (acc_xxx) to call the method on behalf of.

patch.description:
Partially updates the specified User profile. Use `me` as `user_id` to update the account owner profile. Omitted properties remain unchanged; supplied values replace existing values; empty strings clear supported text fields; and null deletes nullable singleton resources.

Multipart supported, refer to Sending Files.

get.description: Returns whether the specified User is currently online, identified by the id returned by the provider. Only supported by Instagram, LinkedIn, Telegram and WhatsApp. A User whose provider reports no presence at all is returned as `unknown`, and Instagram and WhatsApp never report the presence of the account owner. Instagram also only shares the presence of other Users when the account shares its own activity status.

parameters.description: The ID of the User whose presence must be retrieved, as returned by the provider. Use `me` to specify the owner of the connected account, although providers do not always report the presence of the account owner.

parameters.description: ID of the Account (acc_xxx) to call the method on behalf of.

import unipile

ACCOUNT_ID = "acc_123456789"

configuration = unipile.Configuration()
configuration.api_key["apiKey"] = "YOUR_API_KEY"

with unipile.ApiClient(configuration) as api_client:

    'user_id',
    ACCOUNT_ID
)

user_id.description: The ID of the User this presence belongs to.

presence.description:
Whether the user is currently connected to the provider.
    - `online` if the user is connected right now.
    - `offline` if the user is not connected. `last_online_at` is set when the provider exposes the exact date.
    - `unknown` if the provider reports no presence for this user, which usually means the user hides it.

last_online_at.description: Date and time when the user was last online. Only set when the user is offline and the provider exposes the exact date.

provider.description:
The provider's of the Account.
    - `mock` is mock.
    - `whatsapp` is WhatsApp.
    - `linkedin` is LinkedIn.
    - `instagram` is Instagram.
    - `facebook` is Facebook.
    - `google` is Google.
    - `outlook` is Outlook.
    - `telegram` is Telegram.
    - `imap` is IMAP.

get.description:
Returns the list of reactions made by a user to posts. Use `me` as `user_id` to specify the owner of the connected account.
      LIMITATIONS: On Facebook, only the account itself (`me`) or one of its activated Pages can be listed, with at most 25 reactions per page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: An offset used for pagination, if supported by the provider, else use `cursor`.

parameters.description: A cursor used for pagination. If supported by the provider, use `next_cursor` given by the previous page of the list, else use `offset`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The limit of items to be returned. The maximum allowed value depends on the provider. This is a ceiling, not a guarantee: some providers can return fewer items than requested for a given page.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: The ID of the User to retrieve the reactions from.

parameters.description: ID of the Account (acc_xxx) to call the method on behalf of.

post.description: Occurs when an account or one of its products has a service interruption due to an issue or outage with Unipile, the provider, or a proxy service. [Learn more about account status.](https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/docs/status-lifecycle)

post.description:
Occurs when an email is upserted in a folder:

* A received email is upserted in the Inbox folder
* A sent email is upserted in the Outbox (Sent items)
* An email moved from one folder to another is upserted in the new folder

Occurs when an email is deleted from a folder. Note that this event is also triggered when an email is moved from one folder to another as it's deleted from its original folder.

apiKey.description: API key created in the Unipile dashboard or with the API Keys methods. Use a key belonging to the same Application as the targeted Account.

Error.description: RFC 7807 problem object returned for every error.

type.description: Error type, `thrower/info` where thrower is `api` (Unipile) or `provider` (forwarded).

req_id.description: Request identifier, useful when contacting support.

id.description: Identifier of the event (evt_xxx).

created_at.description: Date time the event was created by Unipile.

account_id.description: Identifier of the account for which the event occurs (acc_xxx).

account_scope_id.description: Identifier of the parent scope of the account (scope_xxx).

application_id.description: Identifier of the account's parent application (app_xxx).

application_production.description: Whether the parent application is a production environment.

type.description: Type of the event (`resource.event`).

object.description: The type of the returned object.

user_id.description: The ID of the user that owns the account for the provider.

name.description: The name of the account. This is usually the display name or public identifier (phone number, email address, etc.) of the user that owns the account.

created_at.description: The date and time the account was linked with Unipile.

id.description: ID of the account.

account_scope_id.description: ID of the Scope assigned to the Account. Once assigned, the Scope cannot be removed or replaced.

status.description:
The current status of the account.
    - `running` is Operational.
    - `errored` is Service Interuption.
    - `disconnected` requires authentication.
    - `degraded` means at least one product is running while another is errored; inspect `metadata.products_connection_status`.
    - `partial` means at least one product is running while another requires authentication; inspect `metadata.products_connection_status`.
    Learn more about [Status & Lifecycle](https://developer.unipile.com/v2.0/docs/status-lifecycle).

is_locked.description: Whether API access to the account is locked.

provider.description:
The provider's of the Account.
    - `mock` is mock.
    - `whatsapp` is WhatsApp.
    - `linkedin` is LinkedIn.
    - `instagram` is Instagram.
    - `facebook` is Facebook.
    - `google` is Google.
    - `outlook` is Outlook.
    - `telegram` is Telegram.
    - `imap` is IMAP.

oauth_scope.description: If the provider is OAuth, this is the scope of comma-separated permissions granted to the account.

auto_proxy_country.description: The preferred country for automatic proxy selection. A country inferred from an IP may be outside Unipile’s proxy offering. The current proxy may be in another country when fallback is allowed and no proxy is available in the preferred country.

allow_country_fallback.description: Whether an available proxy from another country may be used when none is available in the rotation country, during authentication and throughout the account lifetime. Defaults to true. A country included in Unipile’s proxy offering may still have no proxy currently available. If false, authentication fails when no proxy is available in the rotation country. If the selected proxy later fails and no replacement is available there, the account enters Service interruption. Rotation to another available proxy in that country remains allowed.

connection_method.description: The authentication method that currently owns the account session lifecycle.

v1_account_id.description: The ID of the account in the v1 if the account is migrated from v1.

v1_instance_port.description: The port of the v1 instance from which the account was migrated.

products_connection_status.description: The status of the connection to a product, if the account is connected to multiple products.

products_display_names.description: The human-readable name of a product, keyed like products_connection_status, when the product has one (e.g. the name of a Facebook Page).

custom_data.description: Custom data of the account. This is where you can store custom data using "Update an account" method.

initial_sync.description: Sync details if the account has initial sync enabled.

status.description:
The state of an account’s initial provider sync.
  - `pending`sync hasn’t started yet.
  - `running` sync is currently in progress.
  - `failed` sync could not be completed due to an error.
  - `completed` sync finished successfully.
  .

started_at.description: The date and time the initial sync started.

proxy.description: The proxy used for the account.

country.description: The country of the proxy. If null, the proxy has no defined country.

auto_proxy.description: Whether the proxy was set automatically by Unipile.

host.description: The host of the custom proxy.

port.description: The port of the custom proxy.

username.description: The username used to authenticate to the custom proxy.

protocol.description: The protocol of the custom proxy.

has_more.description: Whether there are more accounts to fetch.

id.description: The ID of the email.

message_id.description: The Message-ID header value of the email. Use `id` in Unipile requests.

thread_id.description: The thread identifier. For IMAP, Unipile uses the server-provided thread ID when available. Otherwise, it uses the entire References header, or In-Reply-To, or Message-ID, in that order. A header-derived value may differ between messages in the same conversation and may be absent when none of these headers exists.

body.description: The complete body of the email: HTML when available, otherwise plain text. An empty string when the email has no body or meta_only=true.

body_plain.description: The complete plain-text body of the email. Uses the original plain-text version when available, otherwise text converted from HTML. For Outlook, text is converted from the HTML body returned by Microsoft Graph, or taken directly from its plain-text body. An empty string when the email has no body or meta_only=true.

snippet.description: A short preview of the email, not its complete plain-text body. Use body_plain for the full text.

headers.description: List of headers. A single email can sometimes have multiple headers with the same key name. Unipile adds all of the headers to the headers array without merging or de-duplicating the data. When the headers contain encoded data, Unipile adds it to the headers array without decoding it.

role.description: The folder role represents a supported special-use purpose (based on RFC special-use attributes where applicable); it does not indicate whether the folder is system-created. Gmail can expose system labels beyond the RFC special-use list: these have is_system=true but no role when they do not map to a supported special-use purpose, such as CATEGORY_* labels. chat_id.description: The ID of the chat where the message was sent.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the message. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

is_sender.description: Is the current user the sender of the message.

is_hidden.description: Is the message hidden. Hidden messages are usually not displayed in the chat but can be as last message is chats list.

is_seen.description: Is the message seen by other participants.

is_delivered.description: Is the message delivered to the other participants.

is_deleted.description: Is the message deleted. Some providers show the message as deleted in the chat.

is_edited.description: Is the message edited. Some providers adds an "edited" mark on the message in the chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the message pinned. Pinned messages are usually displayed at the top of the chat.

is_starred.description: Whether the account has starred the message. This state is private to the account. Absent when unavailable or unsupported.

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

event_type.description:
The type of message event.
    0 : Unknown (Not implemented)
    1 : Chat name update
    2 : Chat description update
    3 : New participant added to the chat group
    4 : Participant kicked or left the chat group
    5 : A message is pinned
    6 : Permissions have been updated
    7 : Participant was promoted or demoted
    8 : Reaction
    9 : Call Missed
    10 : Call Started
    11 : Call Ended
    12 : Call Rejected
    13 : Scheduled Call Created
    14 : Scheduled Call Cancelled
    15 : Scheduled Call Started
    16 : Announcement
    17 : Content mention

location.description: The geographical location of the user.

network_distance.description:
Network distance to a User.
      `SELF`: Yourself.
      `FIRST_DEGREE`: 1st degree connection.
      `SECOND_DEGREE`: 2nd degree connection (connection of a 1st degree).

is_following.description: Whether the current user follows the user.

followers_count.description: The number of followers of the user.

relations_count.description: The number of relations of the user.

shared_relations_count.description: The number of relations that you share with the user.

website_url.description: The URL of the website provided by the user.

portfolio_url.description: The URL of the portfolio provided by the user.

services_page_url.description: The LinkedIn internal URL of the user's services page.

is_premium.description: Whether the User has a premium account.

is_verified.description: Whether the User has a verified account.

interactive.description: WhatsApp interactive content available in the received provider payload. The body is exposed in text. Supports buttons, templates and native flows; missing or unsupported payloads cannot be reconstructed. Button metadata does not imply that Unipile can execute the action.

id.description: Provider button identifier, when available.

text.description: Button label, when available.

name.description: Native flow action name. Unknown actions are not interpreted.

id.description: Provider button identifier, when available.

text.description: Button label, when available.

name.description: Native flow action name. Unknown actions are not interpreted.

album_id.description: Identifier of the media album the message belongs to. Messages sent together as one album share the same value. Can be used as `quote_id` to reply to the whole album. Absent when the message is not part of an album.

id.description: The unique identifier of the chat for the provider.

name.description: The name / title of the chat. If the provider does not provide a name, name is built out of participants usernames.

label.description: If supported by the provider, a label associated with the chat.

description.description: The description / subject of the chat.

public_picture_url.description: Public URL of the chat picture.

private_picture_download_url.description: Private URL to download the chat picture. This URL requires authentication.

image_url.description: The URL of the chat image. Use public_picture_url or private_picture_download_url instead.

created_at.description: The creation date of the chat. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

updated_at.description: The last update date of the chat. Use ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). Some providers update this field on new messages.

last_message_timestamp.description: The timestamp of the last message in the chat. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

muted_until.description: The date until the chat is muted. Use ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ). Is `true` if muted indefinitely.

creator_id.description: The ID of the user who created the chat.

user_id.description: The ID of the other participant in the chat if 1to1 chat.

is_group.description: Is the chat a group chat.

is_channel.description: Is the chat a channel chat.

type.description:
The type of the chat.
    - `group` is a group chat.
    - `1to1` is a 1to1 chat.
    - `channel` is a channel chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the chat pinned at the top of the list, if supported by the provider.

is_readonly.description: Is the chat read-only for the current user. Trying to send messages in read-only chats will fail.

is_archived.description: Is the chat archived. Archived chats are usually hidden from the chat list.

disappearing_messages_timer.description:
The disappearing-message setting for the conversation: `off` when disabled, `seen` when messages disappear after they are seen, or a retention delay in seconds.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the setting.
    This describes the retention of the whole conversation, and is distinct from a message `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

folders.description: A list of folders the chat belongs to.

participants_count.description: The number of participants in the chat if the chat is a group.

unread_count.description: The number of unread messages in the chat. `0` if the chat is read, `-1` if the chat was manually marked as unread by the user and does not have any unread messages.

restrictions.description:
List of action restrictions of the chat.
      - `send_message` is the permission to send messages.

last_message.description: The last message in the chat.

id.description: The ID of the message.

text.description: The text content of the message.

sender_display_name.description: The display name of the sender of the message.

is_sender.description: Is the message sent by the current user.

text.description: The text content of the message.

sender_id.description: The ID of the user who sent the message.

chat_id.description: The ID of the chat where the message was sent.

timestamp.description: The timestamp of the message. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).

is_sender.description: Is the current user the sender of the message.

is_hidden.description: Is the message hidden. Hidden messages are usually not displayed in the chat but can be as last message is chats list.

is_seen.description: Is the message seen by other participants.

is_delivered.description: Is the message delivered to the other participants.

is_deleted.description: Is the message deleted. Some providers show the message as deleted in the chat.

is_edited.description: Is the message edited. Some providers adds an "edited" mark on the message in the chat.

is_pinned.description: Is the message pinned. Pinned messages are usually displayed at the top of the chat.

is_starred.description: Whether the account has starred the message. This state is private to the account. Absent when unavailable or unsupported.

is_event.description: Is the message an event. Events are special messages that are not displayed in the chat but can be used to trigger actions.

is_mentionned.description: Is the message mentionning the current user. Usually to notify.

view_mode.description:
How the ephemeral content of this message may be viewed: `once` for a single opening, `replayable` when the sender allowed it to be opened again.
    Absent when the message is not ephemeral at all - a provider that does not expose the notion, or content the sender chose to keep in the conversation.
    Depending on the provider the media may never be delivered: WhatsApp only ever serves it to the phone that owns the account, in which case the attachment is reported with `is_unavailable` and cannot be downloaded.

is_disappearing.description:
Is the message part of a disappearing conversation, where the provider automatically deletes messages for every participant once the conversation retention delay has elapsed.
    Absent when the provider does not expose the notion.
    This describes the retention of the conversation the message belongs to, and is distinct from `view_mode`, which describes a single piece of content the recipient may only open a limited number of times.

expires_at.description:
The date at which a disappearing message is automatically deleted. Uses ISO 8601 UTC datetime (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ).
    Absent when the message is not disappearing, or when the provider does not expose enough information to determine the date.

event_type.description:
The type of message event.
    0 : Unknown (Not implemented)
    1 : Chat name update
    2 : Chat description update
    3 : New participant added to the chat group
    4 : Participant kicked or left the chat group
    5 : A message is pinned
    6 : Permissions have been updated
    7 : Participant was promoted or demoted
    8 : Reaction
    9 : Call Missed
    10 : Call Started
    11 : Call Ended
    12 : Call Rejected
    13 : Scheduled Call Created
    14 : Scheduled Call Cancelled
    15 : Scheduled Call Started
    16 : Announcement
    17 : Content mention

Type of the attendee.
          - `required` is a required attendee.
          - `optional` is an optional attendee.
          - `resource` is a resource attendee like a room or a device.

response_status.description:
The response status of the attendee.
          - `yes` if the invitation is accepted.
          - `no` if the invitation is declined.
          - `maybe` if the attendee is not sure.
          - `noreply` if the invitation is pending.

The conference provider.

        - `zoom` is a Zoom conference.
        - `skype` is a Skype conference.
        - `teams` is a Microsoft Teams conference.
        - `unknown` is an unknown conference provider.

hosting.description:
How the conference is attached to the event.
        - `native`: hosted by the calendar provider (Microsoft Teams or Skype on Outlook, Google Meet on Google). The
          provider owns the meeting and `url` is its join link.
        - `description`: an existing conference attached by URL, whose join link is published in the event body.

url.description: The URL used to join the conference.

visibility.description:
The visibility of the event.
        - `public` is visible to all.
        - `private` is visible only to the calendar owner.

transparency.description:
The transparency of the event.
        - `opaque` does block time on the calendar and is equivalent to setting Show me as to Busy in the Calendar UI.
        - `transparent` does not block time on the calendar and is equivalent to setting Show me as to Available in the Calendar UI.

timezone.description: The IANA timezone when start and end share the same timezone (e.g. `Europe/Paris`). Omitted when they differ; use `start.timezone` and `end.timezone` instead.
